description: Doris Stanley recalls watching television coverage of the September 11 attacks while working at a restaurant as a 21-year-old. As the restaurant prepared to open for lunch, its televisions switched to footage of the attacks in New York, Pennsylvania, and at the Pentagon. She remembers watching the World Trade Center collapse and describes feeling shocked and frightened as the footage played repeatedly. Stanley says the television coverage had effects she recognized later, including anxiety, panic attacks, and new fears of heights and driving over bridges. After coming to UCF, she used counseling services and says she connected those experiences to watching the coverage. During a later visit to New York for a conference, she went to the memorial and describes the visit as healing in some ways. Recorded September 11, 2026, this interview is part of the UCF Remembers 9/11 collection.
